items.title: 60499_Garvin Bushell oral history interview
items.q: He'd be there by himself, W. K. Vanderbilt, and we'd sit up and play a couple tunes and he'd sit there listening, tapping his feet.

ctx.x: He always told me, "Bring that fat one, the one that plays that organ." Vanderbilt would invite us out to his house just by -- nobody there, no party -- he'd say, "Garvin, what are you doing today?" "Nothing." "Can you bring four or five guys out -- and bring that fat one?" "All right." "Come on out to the house." "When do you want us?" "Soon as you can get here." I'd get the guys together and I'd get Fats and a drummer and myself and we'd go out to his house. He'd be there by himself, W. K. Vanderbilt, and we'd…

died, they said, of a broken heart. He used -- very often he'd say to us, "I have you boys out here because you're genuine and if I could have just half the fun that you guys have, but I can't because everybody B.S.'s me. I don't who's genuine, who means what they say in my own family." He was the most miserable man -- then he had over $300 million. So, Fats used to say, "Mr. Vanderbilt, you give me some of your money, I'll show you how to have fun." And that would knock him out. That would kill him.
